authority.scope: investigation, reconciliation, and synthetic evidence only

prerequisiteTickets.priorEvidence: Release ordering placed the remote deploy before saving deployment identity; prior source inspection identified no lookup or reconciliation operation.
prerequisiteTickets.newObservation: Each lost or indeterminate response made one deployment attempt and one rollback attempt, then held without resuming verification. A killed controller stayed fenced until verified lease recovery, then issued a second deployment and verified that second identity.
prerequisiteTickets.unreachable: Provider lookup, alias reconciliation, and one-call verification resume are not represented by the current release adapter.
prerequisiteTickets.futureAcceptance: After implementation, lose the response and kill after remote success; restart through the normal entry point and require one remote deployment, reconciled identity, retained rollback target, all nine production checks, and LIVE proof for that identity.

prerequisiteTickets.priorEvidence: The controller had aggregate REFINING and VALIDATING packets plus approval-level stale-evidence checks.
prerequisiteTickets.newObservation: Approval reuse and coarse invalidation worked, and negative, missing, and inapplicable observations blocked. An accepted sub-activity could not be resumed because the state names no activity identity.
prerequisiteTickets.unreachable: Selecting the earliest unfinished editorial or presentation activity is impossible through the current aggregate stage contract.
prerequisiteTickets.futureAcceptance: Interrupt after each accepted activity, restart normally, and assert ordered next-activity dispatch, no repeated accepted worker call, stale-receipt invalidation, and explicit treatment of missing or inapplicable observations.

prerequisiteTickets.priorEvidence: A selected failing review blocked and exact rejected execution bytes remained readable.
prerequisiteTickets.newObservation: An unchanged resubmission was rejected, but a separate passing review could omit or merely label the prior finding resolved and advance. Repair instructions stayed generic.
prerequisiteTickets.unreachable: Stable finding identity, evidenced repair, appropriate removal, evidenced dismissal, owner adjudication, and affected-regression records are absent from current schemas.
prerequisiteTickets.futureAcceptance: Carry a finding ID, criterion, revision, original observation, changed input, resolution type, independent check, and affected regression set through rejection, repair, fresh review, and closure.

prerequisiteTickets.priorEvidence: Stage-wide repair totals and a diagnosis gate existed.
prerequisiteTickets.newObservation: Totals reached three across changed finding, worker, and session labels and survived reload. Error routing changed with wording; diagnosis lacked prediction and disproof fields; one opaque record could satisfy both recovery and remedy evidence; measurement changes were not classified.
prerequisiteTickets.unreachable: A separately verified remedy and independent measurement-change approval cannot be recorded by current contracts.
prerequisiteTickets.futureAcceptance: Vary wording without changing category, reach three cumulative failures across identities, require a falsifiable diagnosis plus distinct remedy check, and independently approve threshold or viewport changes before another attempt.

prerequisiteTickets.priorEvidence: Cached output still passed through validation, and lease recovery required verified owner exit.
prerequisiteTickets.newObservation: Interrupted and intentional repair work reused the same packet identity. No predecessor, replacement, candidate provenance, or selection reason exists. Lease fencing worked in the tested process-exit case.
prerequisiteTickets.unreachable: A late attempt A arriving while replacement B is active cannot be represented because B has no distinct identity or result slot.
prerequisiteTickets.futureAcceptance: Give intentional repair B a new identity linked to A, deliver A late, keep A historical by default, record any reuse decision against inputs and open findings, then rerun validation and independent review.

prerequisiteTickets.priorEvidence: The research registry validated relevance, support, integrity, and freshness; the generic frozen graph retained exact referenced bytes.
prerequisiteTickets.newObservation: Each research dimension failed closed independently, missing/stale/invalid research recovered through the controller, and seeded dependent approvals were invalidated while their bytes stayed readable. Only research exercised a first-class canonical register boundary.
prerequisiteTickets.unreachable: First-class registration for findings, resolutions, editorial judgments, browser observations, and production proof, plus an independently surviving approval, is absent from the current product contract.
prerequisiteTickets.futureAcceptance: Exercise every evidence class through its implemented register boundary, preserve unknown history as unknown, bind fresh judgment to the examined revision, and prove dependency-based invalidation and justified independent survival separately.

prerequisiteTickets.priorEvidence: Catalogue serving and mutable import completion were known to have separate admission paths.
prerequisiteTickets.newObservation: The real public route component and an isolated Next HTTP server served the approved synthetic catalogue at 200 even after a separate mutable import changed. Five one-at-a-time input changes showed safe but over-broad presentation invalidation. Direct approval and validator probes rejected an artifact mismatch, an intended-versus-observed deployment commit mismatch, and retained production proof for the wrong deployment.
prerequisiteTickets.unreachable: No single current reconciler compares served revision, approval, intended commit, production observation, and terminal identity after the fact.
prerequisiteTickets.futureAcceptance: Run target and unaffected control through catalogue and import paths, vary content, renderer, styles, asset, and rules, then require one reconciliation record to justify reuse or revalidation and refuse LIVE on any five-identity disagreement.

prerequisiteTickets.priorEvidence: The controller had distinct pre-publication repair and post-publication IMPROVE paths.
prerequisiteTickets.newObservation: A release acceptance failure retained pending release state and created no LIVE or IMPROVE proof. A synthetic post-LIVE correction preserved original acceptance bytes and required before/after, regression, and independent-review evidence.
prerequisiteTickets.unreachable: Pre-publication repair cannot name a more precise owner or obligation than the productive stage and a generic message.
prerequisiteTickets.futureAcceptance: Fail a named required check before publication and route it to the owning activity; separately correct a post-LIVE defect through IMPROVE while proving the original publication history is byte-identical.

prerequisiteTickets.priorEvidence: Work packets embedded the full import record and frozen references could remain readable by hash.
prerequisiteTickets.newObservation: No explicit handoff or disposal declaration exists, and an incomplete-cleanup marker did not block dispatch. A test-only controlled-time classifier illustrated expected dispositions only.
prerequisiteTickets.unreachable: Later-gate cleanup, explicit manual cleanup, per-gate archive registration, expiry recheck, trigger parity, retry-state preservation, and worker-call preservation cannot be exercised through a current controller entry point.
prerequisiteTickets.futureAcceptance: Use the same durable operation for automatic and manual triggers, classify every item, preserve retry identity and counts, recheck day-30 eligibility and new dependencies, and block dispatch until readable next inputs are verified.

prerequisiteTickets.priorEvidence: A marker probe showed the absence of a cleanup barrier; generic transient and shared-integrity strategies existed.
prerequisiteTickets.newObservation: All three Q44 crash markers were ignored, uncertain bytes did not hold dispatch, and the generic stage transient count reached three without operation-scoped exhaustion. A shared integrity code stopped immediately.
prerequisiteTickets.unreachable: Crash recovery after registered intent, archive copy, or reference registration is impossible until cleanup operation state exists.
prerequisiteTickets.futureAcceptance: Interrupt the same operation at all three boundaries, reconcile bytes and references before mutation or dispatch, preserve authoring identity, exhaust exactly three pre-mutation temporary attempts across restarts, and require a verified remedy.

prerequisiteTickets.priorEvidence: Supplied verdict fixtures tested controller behavior but did not test reviewer recognition.
prerequisiteTickets.newObservation: Six fresh blinded reviewers correctly accepted three adequate controls and rejected the paired CTA, semantic-fidelity, and keyboard-scroll defects, each with evidence-matching explanations.
prerequisiteTickets.unreachable: The six cases cannot establish general reviewer reliability or historical WebCatalog review provenance.
prerequisiteTickets.futureAcceptance: Retain these six as the minimum reviewer boundary, rerun them unchanged against the future reviewer configuration, and add only finding-specific controls needed by the authorized implementation.

prerequisiteTickets.priorEvidence: Release-era records, later rewrite records, fresh 27 November judgments, and current tests were bounded and classified separately.
prerequisiteTickets.newObservation: All 38 findings were mapped to source, purpose, format, owner, actual retained observation, current coverage, and causal confidence. The 27 November live-page inventory has a date and mutable public URL but no commit, deployment identity, or capture fingerprint, so its exact revision binding is unavailable. Later issue 107 evidence supplies revision-bound reviewer-effectiveness results for findings 12, 19, and 31 only.
prerequisiteTickets.unreachable: Missing historical review provenance cannot be recreated by a fresh judgment, and many current tests cannot prove release-era execution.
prerequisiteTickets.futureAcceptance: Use the 38-row inventory as the demonstration ledger, bind every fresh observation to the demonstrated revision, retain pass and fail evidence, and keep historical disposition separate from the new run.

testingDecisions.evidence: Issues 98-102 and 104-106 exercise controller or supervised-executor seams with persisted synthetic state. Issue 103 exercises the HTTP route, approval contracts, release adapter, and validators directly; it is not a supervised restart test. None substitutes for future implemented paths.
Issue 99 exercises omission, unchanged submission, inconclusive review, and currently unrepresentable resolution types.
Issues 105-106 prove the barrier is absent; crash recovery remains future acceptance.
Issue 97 records lost response, process exit, remote calls, journal, rollback target, and outstanding verification.
Issue 107 retains six blinded defective/adequate review packets and judgments.
Issue 108 maps all 38 findings and this reconciliation adds issue 107's later reviewer results.
Issues 98 and 100 cover restart, repair totals, wording, missing observations, and measurement changes; several intended states remain unrepresentable.
Issue 102 exercises research registration and records unreachable canonical evidence classes separately.
Issues 103-104 cover catalogue/import scope and pre-publication versus IMPROVE history.
Issues 105-106 inventory current handoff/retention behavior and preserve test-only classification as expected behavior only.
Every prerequisite separates prior evidence, new observation, unreachable state, and future acceptance; supplied verdicts are not counted as reviewer effectiveness.

interviewCoverage.evidence: Issue 108 maps source, purpose, applicability, owner, checks, gaps, and causation for 38 findings.
Issues 98-100 cover checkpoints, rejection, routing, invalidation, missing observation, and bounded recovery.
Issues 97, 103, and 104 cover LIVE agreement, publication paths, affected scope, remote outcome, repair, and IMPROVE.
Issues 99 and 107 separate finding continuity from six blinded judgments.
Issues 100-101 cover repair relevance, identities, diagnosis, regression, counts, measurement changes, categories, and late output.
Issues 102, 105, and 106 cover protected references, per-gate cleanup, handoff, barrier, dispositions, and 30-day retention.
Legacy access, current compliance, and routing of legacy defects require owner adjudication only when a concrete case needs it.
